classification.difficultyReason: Identify horizontal and vertical right triangles, calculate their sides and use an inverse trigonometric ratio.

content.prompt: $AEFD$ is a horizontal rectangle. $ABCD$ is a rectangle inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. $AD=32\text{ cm}$, $AE=24\text{ cm}$ and $BE=41\text{ cm}$. Find, correct to one decimal place where necessary:

spec.description: Inclined rectangle ABCD shares AD with horizontal rectangle AEFD. B and C lie vertically above E and F. AE, EF and BE are dashed; remaining edges are solid. Ordinary source blue and red strokes are house black, with the dashed visibility distinction retained. No face shading.
spec.mathematics: AD=32 cm, AE=DF=24 cm, BE=CF=41 cm. Theta is angle CDF. The right-angle cue at F is between FC and FE.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, point labels, inclination angle and right-angle cue are shown; no requested diagonal or answer is added.

answer.worked:
The corresponding vertical edges have equal lengths, so $CF=BE=41\text{ cm}$. Also, $DF=AE=24\text{ cm}$. In right-angled triangle $DCF$:
$$\begin{align*}DC^2&=DF^2+CF^2\\DC^2&=24^2+41^2\\DC^2&=2257\\DC&=\sqrt{2257}\text{ cm}\\DC&\approx47.5\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

In the horizontal rectangle, triangle $ADF$ is right-angled at $D$:
$$\begin{align*}AF^2&=AD^2+DF^2\\AF^2&=32^2+24^2\\AF^2&=1600\\AF&=40\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

Since $CF$ is perpendicular to the horizontal plane, triangle $ACF$ is right-angled at $F$:
$$\begin{align*}\tan\angle CAF&=\frac{CF}{AF}\\\tan\angle CAF&=\frac{41}{40}\\\angle CAF&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{41}{40}\right)\\\angle CAF&\approx45.7^\circ.\end{align*}$$
